                               REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE                       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    This chapter presents a review of related literature, articles, and studies that
                                                                                  
               provided proper guidelines for creating and formulating the requirements needed to
               start the project. Moreover, the chapter was designed to examine the literature in the
                                                                                  
               field, and researchers gained insights into the key concepts, methodologies,
                                                                                  
               challenges, and best practices associated with the development and utilization of
                                                                                  
               such systems.                                                      
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Related Foreign Literature                                         
                                                                                  
               Real-Time Vehicle Tracking for Passenger Awareness                 
                                                                                  
                    Almeida et al. (2023) explored how real-time tracking of public vehicles
                                                                                  
               (specifically city buses) can be leveraged to characterize traffic congestion and
                                                                                  
               enhance passenger information systems. In Aveiro, Portugal, there has been a
                                                                                  
               collection of four weeks' worth of bus tracking data, which was used by the authors
                                                                                  
               as a basis for how average speed, travel time, delays, and number of stops can
                                                                                  
               serve as indicators of traffic conditions. By using clustering techniques like DBSCAN
                                                                                  
               and k-means, three levels of congestion have been identified. The authors mapped
                                                                                  
               how congestion evolves over different times of the day and across segments of an
                                                                                  
               urban network                                                      
                                                                                  
                    Based on the results, it shows that real-time tracking data not only helps
                                                                                  
               detect zones and times of consistent congestion, but it also gives feedback for
               commuters and planners. Therefore, in practice, systems similar to this reduce
                                                                                  
               uncertainty of arrival times and waiting durations, directly improving commuter
                                                                                  
               satisfaction and trust in the public transit system. The study emphasized the
                                                                                  
               criticalness of transparency and data availability. When people can see vehicle
                                                                                  
               locations and expected times, their commute becomes more efficient and reliable.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 37 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      16          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Near Field Communication (NFC) in Public Transportation Security   
                                                                                  
                    A 2024 report by NFC Tagify explored how Near Field Communication (NFC)
                                                                                  
               is modernizing public transportation, turning it into a more secure and efficient
                                                                                  
               experience. By replacing traditional paper tickets with contactless cards and mobile
               payments, NFC technology dramatically speeds up transaction times and reduces
                                                                                  
               long queues during rush hour. This shift not only cuts down on manual ticket
                                                                                  
               inspections and fare fraud, but it also shows how public transit is adapting to today's
                                                                                  
               digital landscape.                                                 
                                                                                  
                    Beyond efficiency, NFC brings a much-needed layer of security to transit
                                                                                  
               systems. The technology relies on encrypted communication, making it extremely
                                                                                  
               difficult for bad actors to duplicate tickets or tamper with terminal data. Furthermore,
                                                                                  
               real-time tracking of passenger flow allows transit authorities to monitor crowds and
                                                                                  
               quickly address any unusual activity. For passengers, the integration of mobile apps
                                                                                  
               makes the process completely transparent, allowing them to store tickets and review
                                                                                  
               their ride history with ease. While challenges like high installation costs and
                                                                                  
               cybersecurity threats remain, NFC is proving to be a game-changer in building safer,
                                                                                  
               smarter, and more user-friendly transportation networks.           
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Crowd-Sourced Traffic Data: The Case of Waze                       
                                                                                  
                    Burch et al. (2022) presented an interactive public transport navigation
                                                                                  
               system that integrates dynamic passenger data into transit maps to assist users in
                                                                                  
               route planning. Rather than relying solely on static maps, their system visualizes
               real-time and historical data such as passenger counts, station usage, and temporal
                                                                                  
               patterns across different granularity levels. The addition of density plots, calendar
                                                                                  
               views, and line graphs layered onto the transit map allows users to intuitively assess
                                                                                  
               how crowded certain routes or stations tend to be at various times. In a user
                                                                                  
               experiment with 20 non-expert participants, they found that the enhanced maps
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 38 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      17          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               helped people identify less crowded travel times or routes, without significantly
                                                                                  
               increasing the time it took participants to find a route compared to traditional maps.
                                                                                  
                    Although the paper does not directly analyze crowd-sourced applications like
                                                                                  
               Waze, it demonstrates how transparent access to passenger and mobility data can
               improve commuter confidence, reduce uncertainty, and support better
                                                                                  
               decision-making. In this sense, it aligns with the idea of collective intelligence and
                                                                                  
               user participation in traffic systems. The study also discusses scalability challenges
                                                                                  
               (e.g., visual clutter, data integration, and maintaining robust performance as the data
                                                                                  
               size grows), which are relevant considerations for adapting such systems to more
                                                                                  
               complex or data-poor cities.                                       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Real-Time Vehicle Tracking for Fleet Optimization                  
                                                                                  
                    Liu Aemmer et al. (2022) highlighted the importance of real-time vehicle
                                                                                  
               tracking in creating public transit systems that serve both commuters and transport
                                                                                  
               operators efficiently. Their study emphasized that live tracking of vehicles helps close
                                                                                  
               the gap between scheduled dispatch plans and actual on-road performance. By
                                                                                  
               providing operators with real-time information about their fleet, transit services can
                                                                                  
               move away from guesswork and make informed decisions that optimize routes,
                                                                                  
               reduce delays, and improve overall efficiency.                     
                                                                                  
                    This concept is particularly relevant for cooperative and local transport
                                                                                  
               systems, such as the Pangkabuhayan Transport Service Multipurpose Cooperative
                                                                                  
               (PTSMC). Traditionally, drivers follow strict dispatch rules, often leaving terminals
               with very few passengers, which makes the pickup process uncertain and inefficient.
                                                                                  
               By implementing real-time tracking and monitoring systems, drivers can update seat
                                                                                  
               availability in real time using simple indicators like red, yellow, and green signals.
                                                                                  
               Commuters can see which vehicles have available seats, turning a chance-based
                                                                                  
               system into a proactive and organized strategy. Additionally, management can use
                                                                                  
               web dashboards to monitor fleet activity, track fuel usage, and validate passenger
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 39 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      18          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               numbers. This approach benefits both drivers on the road and operators behind the
                                                                                  
               scenes, improving service reliability, operational efficiency, and passenger
                                                                                  
               satisfaction.                                                      
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Integration of GPS in Urban Mobility                               
                                                                                  
                    Paulsen (2021) examined how GPS technology has been integrated within
                                                                                  
               commuter applications to support location tracking, route planning, and estimated
                                                                                  
               arrival information. His analysis revealed that GPS-based platforms allow transport
                                                                                  
               operators and application developers to reliably monitor vehicle positions, assess
                                                                                  
               route performance, and provide travelers with dynamic, real-time updates on their
                                                                                  
               journeys. Through the precise locational data afforded by GPS, users gain better
                                                                                  
               awareness of their position relative to vehicles or stops, while systems can optimize
                                                                                  
               route assignments or adjust operations in response to traffic conditions.
                                                                                  
                    The study underscored that GPS forms a foundational technological layer for
                                                                                  
               more advanced mobility applications. Without accurate location and timing data,
                                                                                  
               features like live arrival prediction, route deviation alerts, or adaptive scheduling
                                                                                  
               would have limited effectiveness. Paulsen emphasized that the success of many
                                                                                  
               contemporary commuter applications hinges on the robust integration of GPS, which
                                                                                  
               enables transparency in operations and builds user trust in the services. However, he
                                                                                  
               also noted challenges such as signal loss in dense urban canyons, GPS drift in
                                                                                  
               tunnels or underpasses, and the need to pair GPS data with other sensor or
                                                                                  
               contextual data (e.g., accelerometers, map-matching) to improve accuracy. Overall,
               Paulsen’s work helps bridge between the raw technology of GPS and the
                                                                                  
               user-oriented mobility services that rely on it, showing how location intelligence
                                                                                  
               underpins modern urban transport applications.                     
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 40 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      19          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Related Local Literature                                           
                                                                                  
               The Centrality of Automobiles in Transport Planning                
                                                                                  
                    Gatarin (2023) conducted a critical examination of Metro Manila’s transport
                                                                                  
               crisis, emphasizing the entrenched dominance of car-centric planning in government
               infrastructure priorities. Despite the fact that only a minority of Filipinos own and drive
                                                                                  
               private vehicles, most transport investments and policies disproportionately cater to
                                                                                  
               automobiles. The misalignment has produced systemic inefficiencies, fragmented
                                                                                  
               mobility options, and worsening congestion that affects the majority of commuters
                                                                                  
               who depend on buses, trains, jeepneys, and other forms of shared and active
                                                                                  
               transport. By privileging cars, state actors inadvertently marginalize low- and
                                                                                  
               middle-income commuters, reinforcing inequities in access to safe, reliable, and
                                                                                  
               affordable mobility.                                               
                                                                                  
                    Importantly, Gatarin’s analysis highlighted the role of cultural discourses and
                                                                                  
               civil society initiatives in shaping alternative pathways toward sustainable urban
                                                                                  
               mobility. Efforts such as road-sharing projects and grassroots advocacy illustrate how
                                                                                  
               Metro Manila residents are reimagining transport beyond car dominance. The study
                                                                                  
               concludes that a people-centered, process-oriented, and ecologically balanced
                                                                                  
               framework—one that prioritizes moving people rather than cars—offers a more
                                                                                  
               inclusive solution to urban mobility challenges. By reframing responsibility as a
                                                                                  
               shared societal task rather than a purely top-down government mandate, Gatarin’s
                                                                                  
               work underscores both the failures of traditional car-centric planning and the
                                                                                  
               possibilities for more equitable and liveable transport systems in cities of the Global
               South.                                                             
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Mobility Infrastructure in ASEAN: A Philippine Perspective         
                                                                                  
                    Ibrahim (2025) undertakes a comparative evaluation of the Philippines’
                                                                                  
               mobility infrastructure relative to other ASEAN member states, using metrics from the
                                                                                  
               Global Competitiveness Index and related benchmark tools. The study reveals that
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 41 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      20          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               the Philippines significantly trails its regional neighbors in areas such as transport
                                                                                  
               infrastructure consistency, efficiency of ports/airports, railway density, and overall
                                                                                  
               adequacy of mobility networks. The lag is shown to have negative spillovers not only
                                                                                  
               on daily commuters—through longer travel times, congestion, and unreliable
               services—but also on the country’s economic competitiveness in ASEAN and
                                                                                  
               beyond.                                                            
                                                                                  
                    Ibrahim emphasizes that mobility deficits constrain both labor mobility and
                                                                                  
               goods transport, which in turn raise costs for business and reduce attractiveness for
                                                                                  
               investment. He notes that weak public transport efficiency, fragmented networks
                                                                                  
               (e.g., disconnected rail, limited intermodal integration), and underinvestment in
                                                                                  
               supportive infrastructure (stations, feeder networks, last-mile connectivity) are among
                                                                                  
               the main culprits. The study recommends reforms that are comprehensive:
                                                                                  
               modernizing infrastructure (rail, airport, port), improving efficiency and management
                                                                                  
               of existing assets, better planning and coordination across agencies, and investing in
                                                                                  
               public transport accessibility and reliability—all aimed not just at improving commuter
                                                                                  
               convenience, but strengthening national competitiveness and economic inclusion.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Economic Cost of Traffic Congestion in the Philippines             
                                                                                  
                    Punongbayan (2025) analyzed the heavy economic and social toll of Metro
                                                                                  
               Manila’s chronic traffic congestion. His study estimated the cost of traffic delays at
                                                                                  
               ₱3.5 billion per day in 2023, a figure projected to reach ₱5.4 billion daily by 2035 if no
                                                                                  
               reforms are implemented. The costs arise from lost worker productivity, increased
               fuel consumption, higher logistics expenses, and the overall inefficiency of moving
                                                                                  
               people and goods across the metropolis. Framing traffic as both a commuter and a
                                                                                  
               national economic problem, Punongbayan highlighted how congestion undermines
                                                                                  
               household welfare, business competitiveness, and the broader Philippine economy.
                                                                                  
                    The study situated the problem within the country’s decades-long car-centric
                                                                                  
               planning paradigm, in which government investments disproportionately favored road
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 42 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      21          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               expansion and elevated expressways over integrated public transit. Such priorities
                                                                                  
               reinforced car ownership while leaving mass transit systems—rail, buses, and active
                                                                                  
               transport—fragmented, unreliable, and underfunded. Punongbayan emphasized that
                                                                                  
               sustainable solutions require rebalancing mobility priorities by modernizing and
               integrating rail, bus rapid transit, and cycling infrastructure under coherent oversight.
                                                                                  
               Ultimately, the study calls for a shift to people-centered, dignified public transport as a
                                                                                  
               pathway to reducing congestion, improving quality of life, and sustaining economic
                                                                                  
               growth.                                                            
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Infrastructure Investment and Mobility: PIDS Report                
                                                                                  
                    Navarro and Latigar (2022), in a policy study by the Philippine Institute for
                                                                                  
               Development Studies (PIDS) and later cited in Javier (2025), highlighted the chronic
                                                                                  
               underinvestment in Philippine infrastructure. They reported that only 2.5% of the
                                                                                  
               country’s gross domestic product (GDP) is allocated to infrastructure spending—a
                                                                                  
               figure well below global benchmarks. The insufficient investment has contributed to
                                                                                  
               the persistence of poor-quality and inefficient transport systems, particularly in road
                                                                                  
               and rail infrastructure.                                           
                                                                                  
                    The report emphasized that decades of low infrastructure spending have
                                                                                  
               created significant gaps in mobility networks, leaving commuters reliant on
                                                                                  
               inadequate services such as congested roads, limited rail coverage, and insufficient
                                                                                  
               intermodal linkages. The shortcomings not only reduce commuter convenience but
                                                                                  
               also impair economic productivity by increasing travel time, logistics costs, and
               overall inefficiency in the movement of people and goods.          
                                                                                  
                    Javier (2025), in citing Navarro and Latigar, argued that reversing the trend
                                                                                  
               requires sustained and expanded infrastructure investment. Beyond physical
                                                                                  
               expansion, investment should prioritize sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity,
                                                                                  
               ensuring that projects support long-term mobility goals rather than short-term
                                                                                  
               congestion relief. Both the PIDS report and Javier’s analysis converge on the point
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 43 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      22          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               that stronger state commitment to infrastructure spending is essential to enable a
                                                                                  
               modernized, efficient, and people-centered transport system.       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Digital Commuter Assistance: The Case of Sakay.ph                  
                    Sakay.ph is a widely used digital commuter assistance platform in the
                                                                                  
               Philippines that helps users navigate the complex public transportation network of
                                                                                  
               Metro Manila. According to By Implication Inc. (2026), the Sakay.ph mobile
                                                                                  
               application provides commute directions across the National Capital Region by
                                                                                  
               supporting multiple public transportation modes such as jeepneys, regular and P2P
                                                                                  
               buses, MRT, LRT, PNR trains, UV Express, Comet eJeeps, and the Pasig River
                                                                                  
               Ferry. The platform also offers step-by-step commute directions, travel time and cost
                                                                                  
               comparisons, and a crowd-sourced route database, allowing commuters to evaluate
                                                                                  
               available travel options before beginning their trip.              
                                                                                  
                    The relevance of applications such as Sakay.ph is supported by Lara et al.
                                                                                  
               (2024), who emphasized that public transportation navigation in the Philippines
                                                                                  
               remains challenging because commuters often need specific information about
                                                                                  
               routes, fare costs, disembarkation points, and suitable vehicles to reach their
                                                                                  
               destinations. Their study on a routing-based commuter application highlighted the
                                                                                  
               importance of digital tools that provide route suggestions, transportation options,
                                                                                  
               travel cost estimates, and travel time information. These features help commuters
                                                                                  
               make more informed decisions, especially when traveling through unfamiliar areas or
                                                                                  
               using multiple modes of public transportation.                     
                    However, recent local research also indicates that route-planning applications
                                                                                  
               still face limitations related to data accuracy and completeness. Manguan et al.
                                                                                  
               (2026) noted that public transportation in the Philippines is multimodal and
                                                                                  
               demand-responsive, but commuters continue to lack access to real-time and reliable
                                                                                  
               route information. Their study also observed that existing local navigation
                                                                                  
               alternatives, such as Sakay.ph, may experience outdated or incomplete public
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 44 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      23          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               transport data. This limitation is significant because route guidance alone may not
                                                                                  
               fully address commuter uncertainty when vehicle availability, passenger capacity, and
                                                                                  
               operational conditions change in real time.                        
                                                                                  
                    In relation to the present study, Sakay.ph demonstrates the value of digital
               commuter assistance systems in improving route awareness and trip planning.
                                                                                  
               However, its primary focus remains on navigation, route guidance, and travel option
                                                                                  
               comparison. The proposed SureCut system expands these capabilities by integrating
                                                                                  
               real-time vehicle tracking, passenger capacity monitoring, NFC-based cashless
                                                                                  
               payment, and fleet management features. Unlike general route-planning platforms,
                                                                                  
               SureCut is designed to support not only commuters but also Modern Jeepney drivers
                                                                                  
               and transport operators through localized, real-time operational data. These
                                                                                  
               additional features position SureCut as a more comprehensive transportation
                                                                                  
               management solution for the PTSMC route in Bacoor, Cavite.         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Related Foreign Studies                                            
                                                                                  
               Designing and evaluating a smartphone app to increase underserved  
               communities’ data representation in transportation policy and planning
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The article “Designing and Evaluating a Smartphone App to Increase
               Underserved Communities’ Data Representation in Transportation Policy and
                                                                                  
               Planning” by Courtney Cronley et al. (2023) discusses the creation of MyAmble, a
                                                                                  
               mobile application developed to help include voices that are often left out of
                                                                                  
               transportation planning. Traditional systems have long focused on people who own
                                                                                  
               cars, which has resulted in unfair access and outcomes for those who do not. To
                                                                                  
               address the issue, the researchers built MyAmble, an application that records both
                                                                                  
               daily travel routines and the trips people wish they could take but cannot. The project
                                                                                  
               centers on the idea of transportation equity and the value of working with a wide
                                                                                  
               range of community members to design policies that better reflect real experiences
                                                                                  
               and needs.                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 45 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      24          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The MyAmble application was built for Android and includes five main tools:
                                                                                  
               Daily Trip Planner, Trip Review, Challenge Logger, Travel Buddy, and Travel Story.
                                                                                  
               Together, the features allow users to record trips, describe challenges like unsafe
                                                                                  
               sidewalks with photos and GPS tags, and communicate directly with researchers.
               The development process involved close cooperation between experts in social work,
                                                                                  
               engineering, and computer science, along with constant feedback from users. Early
                                                                                  
               tests with older adults and other vulnerable groups helped refine its design, while
                                                                                  
               later focus groups added improvements such as new destination options and more
                                                                                  
               safety details. The final tests showed that MyAmble was easy to use and highlighted
                                                                                  
               how involving stakeholders throughout the process leads to more practical, widely
                                                                                  
               accepted tools for fairer transportation planning.                 
                                                                                  
                    While MyAmble is a passive research tool designed to gather data for future
                                                                                  
               policy-making, SureCut is an active operational tool. SureCut does not record missed
                                                                                  
               trips; but actively prevents them by providing real-time vehicle visibility. Furthermore,
                                                                                  
               SureCut integrates a payment module (NFC) and driver-side capacity management,
                                                                                  
               features absent in MyAmble which focuses solely on the user's travel history and
                                                                                  
               obstacles.                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               GPS Supported Smartphone: App-based Integrated Travel Diary and Time Use
               Data Collection: Challenges and Lessons Learned                    
                                                                                  
                    Maliheh Tabasi et al. (2024) ventured into the intrinsic challenges involved in
                                                                                  
               enlisting participants and gathering good-quality information through GPS-enabled
                                                                                  
               smartphone applications, in addition to imparting useful lessons from a travel and
                                                                                  
               time-use data collection process that was carried out in Chicago and Sydney. The
                                                                                  
               study addressed the usefulness of the Fourstep application, which combines passive
                                                                                  
               location tracking with user entry for activities. The research emphasized that the
                                                                                  
               greatest challenge is still finding and retaining interested participants who will install
                                                                                  
               the application, keep up with interest, and regularly submit rich personal travel
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 46 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      25          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               information, highlighting the importance of the research in creating more suitable
                                                                                  
               travel behavior and time-use models. The Fourstep application itself is a
                                                                                  
               sophisticated tool based on the open-source OpenPath application, tailored for
                                                                                  
               recording rich activity participation data, such as the start/end time, duration, timing,
               sequence, and, most importantly, multitasking behavior, a feature commonly lacking
                                                                                  
               in previous integrated applications.                               
                                                                                  
                    The Fourstep application operates by passively recording movement through
                                                                                  
               GPS and body motion sensors, afterward showing users "trip cards" and "stay cards"
                                                                                  
               upon which they enter granular information, including travel mode, purpose, and
                                                                                  
               activities. The organization, based on trips to structure data input for the day, is
                                                                                  
               overall less onerous compared to standard activity-based diaries even with the
                                                                                  
               complication of the data being harvested. One of the key contributions of the paper is
                                                                                  
               that analysis of successful recruitment methods, specifically the discovery that the
                                                                                  
               first try to recruit the Chicago participants via an expensive international market
                                                                                  
               research firm was not very successful. By contrast, the use of targeted social media
                                                                                  
               advertising was found to be an inexpensive, successful method for the recruitment of
                                                                                  
               the Chicago sample. In addition, the research proved that raising the daily financial
                                                                                  
               incentive caused an abrupt increase in response rates, firmly proving that incentives
                                                                                  
               play an important role in controlling response burden and effectively enrolling
                                                                                  
               participants in elaborate, time-consuming, application-based surveys.
                                                                                  
                    The Fourstep app is designed to study how people use their time during travel
                                                                                  
               and the difficulties of data collection. In contrast, SureCut does not utilize GPS for
               behavioral study, but for immediate navigational utility. While Tabasi’s study highlights
                                                                                  
               the difficulty of retaining users for data collection, SureCut ensures user retention by
                                                                                  
               offering immediate value: real-time arrival estimates and seat availability
                                                                                  
               (Green/Yellow/Red), which Fourstep does not provide.

               BUSNAV: A Real-Time Bus Tracking Application                       
                                                                                  
                    The research introduced the creation of BUSNAV, a next-generation GPS
                                                                                  
               tracking software meant to solve the long time lost by commuters as they wait for
                                                                                  
               buses and the inconvenience caused by the absence of real-time bus arrival
               information. The main aim of Akhade, K. et al. (2024) was to develop a system that
                                                                                  
               would be more accurate and efficient in tracking buses compared to previous ones
                                                                                  
               so as to maximize the public transport experience. BUSNAV was envisioned to be a
                                                                                  
               high-end digital assistant that combines real-time bus location information directly
                                                                                  
               into the familiar user interface of Google Maps using the Google Maps API for easy
                                                                                  
               visualization of routes and locations on an interactive map. The application was
                                                                                  
               developed using a solid methodology, with Java and Kotlin being the technologies
                                                                                  
               used for development, and Firebase acting as the backend infrastructure for real-time
                                                                                  
               data synchronization and storage.                                  
                                                                                  
                    The last BUSNAV application provides a simple interface for navigation
                                                                                  
               through routes, accurate tracking of buses, and the delivery of quick alerts in the
                                                                                  
               event of an emergency. The creation of BUSNAV marks an important milestone
                                                                                  
               toward improving public transportation services by facilitating correct real-time bus
                                                                                  
               tracking and route details. Its ability to minimize passenger waiting times and improve
                                                                                  
               overall efficiency makes it a prime force for change within public transport.
                                                                                  
               Additionally, by providing city planners and policymakers with access to real-time
                                                                                  
               information, the application is set to play a role in larger Smart City initiatives
                                                                                  
               designed to relieve congestion and optimize urban mobility. Overall, the user-oriented
               design and comprehensive data integration utilized by BUSNAV are poised to
                                                                                  
               revolutionize the way transit riders experience public transportation, building a more
                                                                                  
               efficient and accessible future.                                   
                                                                                  
                    BUSNAV shares the same technical foundation as SureCut (Google Maps
                                                                                  
               API + Firebase). However, BUSNAV is tailored for buses with fixed schedules and
                                                                                  
               stops. SureCut innovates by adapting the technology to the flexible nature of Modern
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 48 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      27          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Jeepneys. SureCut includes a Seat Availability Module where drivers manually
                                                                                  
               update occupancy, and an NFC Payment Module, creating a more comprehensive
                                                                                  
               "ride-to-pay" ecosystem that BUSNAV lacks.                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Intelliter: An Android-Based Intelligent Commuting Mobile Application
                                                                                  
                    The paper "Intelliter: An Android-Based Intelligent Commuting Mobile

               commuting system tailored specifically for public utility jeepneys of Angeles City,

               specifically user confusion on the proper jeepney route, which vehicle to take, and
                                                                                  
               the exact fare cost. Addressing the pain points, the system hoped to deliver a more
                                                                                  
               efficient, more reliable, and less effortful travel experience for both new and veteran
                                                                                  
               commuters. The methodology of the application was grounded in the Design
                                                                                  
               Thinking methodology, a very effective, user-centered methodology of
                                                                                  
               problem-solving. Technically, the application was developed as an Android-based
                                                                                  
               system, using a technology stack consisting of XML, Java, Android Studio, and
                                                                                  
               Firebase Realtime to govern its underlying database as well as support real-time
                                                                                  
               data requirements.                                                 
                                                                                  
                    The final prototype of the Intelliter application contained a few key features
                                                                                  
               that specifically catered to commuter demand. These include displaying the user's
                                                                                  
               location in real-time, providing an in-depth guide for one's destination by indicating
                                                                                  
               the jeepneys one should take, presenting the estimated current fare, and mapping
               the particular routes of the jeepneys along Angeles City. The following assessment of
                                                                                  
               the application collected very encouraging feedback from questioned commuters.
                                                                                  
               The system was evaluated against rigorous measures, such as Usability,
                                                                                  
               Functionality, Reliability, and Performance, and scored the top "Strongly Agree" rating
                                                                                  
               consistently on indicators such as user friendliness and general user experience. The
                                                                                  
               research concluded, in the end, that Intelliter is very effective in advising commuters,
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 49 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      28          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               improving the understanding of the public transport system, and offering a
                                                                                  
               cost-effective solution for enhancing the overall efficiency of local traffic.
                                                                                  
                    Intelliter focuses primarily on the commuter's need for information
                                                                                  
               (routes/fares). SureCut advances this by integrating the driver's operational needs.
               SureCut includes a driver module for managing passenger counts and an operator
                                                                                  
               module for fleet oversight. Additionally, SureCut introduces cashless payments via
                                                                                  
               NFC, whereas Intelliter functions mainly as an intelligent guide and fare estimator
                                                                                  
               without a transaction layer.                                       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               G2Viz: An Online Tool for Visualizing and Analyzing Public Transit System from
               GTFS Data                                                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The paper “G2Viz: An Online Tool for Visualizing and Analyzing Public Transit
                                                                                  
               System from GTFS Data” by Sirapop Para et al. (2024), Thanachok Wirotsasithon,
                                                                                  
               and their team discusses the development of a web-based visualization tool
                                                                                  
               designed to help transit agencies and planners better understand public
                                                                                  
               transportation systems. The study highlights the increasing need for tools that can
                                                                                  
               clearly present complex data from older systems, which often depend on mixed and
                                                                                  
               inconsistent sources like Automatic Vehicle Location (AVL) and Automatic Fare
               Collection (AFC). To address the issue, G2Viz utilizes the General Transit Feed
                                                                                  
               Specification (GTFS)—a standardized data format—to simplify transit data analysis.
                                                                                  
               It allows agencies to visualize and evaluate transportation operations more efficiently
                                                                                  
               using existing data, helping improve planning and decision-making. 
                                                                                  
                    According to Para and his co-authors, G2Viz provides visual analytics for
                                                                                  
               important performance indicators such as service rate, vehicle speed, and headway,
                                                                                  
               which refers to the time gap between consecutive vehicles. The paper explains the
                                                                                  
               two main types of GTFS data: GTFS Static, which contains schedule and route
                                                                                  
               information in text files, and GTFS Realtime, which delivers live updates through an
                                                                                  
               API using a different data format. The current version of G2Viz operates primarily
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 50 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      29          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               with GTFS Static data, but the authors suggest that expanding the system to handle
                                                                                  
               GTFS Realtime data would be a valuable direction for future research, potentially
                                                                                  
               offering more accurate and dynamic insights into public transit performance.
                                                                                  
                    G2Viz is a backend analytical tool meant for agencies and planners to study
               system performance. As for SureCut, it is a frontend consumer application. While
                                                                                  
               G2Viz visualizes data for analysis, SureCut visualizes data for immediate
                                                                                  
               action—helping a commuter decide whether to wait for the next jeepney. SureCut
                                                                                  
               also bridges the "digital divide" by giving drivers a simple interface to contribute to the
                                                                                  
               data, whereas G2Viz relies on pre-existing static feeds.
