               conceptual design showed how the PasaHero application interfaced with bus
                                                                                  
               operations and public transport commuters, facilitated by a system architecture that
                                                                                  
               married GPS tracking, cloud-based database, and mobile user interface to offer
                                                                                  
               real-time visibility of bus location and schedules.                
                                                                                  
                    The PasaHero system consisted of three main modules: the Passenger
                                                                                  
               Module to display routes, track buses, and process QR payments; the Driver Module
                                                                                  
               to send GPS information and trip status; and the Admin Module for account
                                                                                  
               management, routes, and reports. The user interface was deliberately made
                                                                                  
               straightforward and interactive to provide accessibility and ease of navigation, a vital

                                                                      30          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               consideration considering the Philippines' diverse mobile network conditions. After
                                                                                  
               development, the system was tested in accordance with ISO/IEC 25010 standards.
                                                                                  
               The outcome showed high performance in functionality and usability, but the system
                                                                                  
               performed worst in reliability, indicating that real-time data accuracy and stability
               require improvements. The research proves the feasibility of leveraging
                                                                                  
               cloud-integrated and location-based applications to enhance commuter convenience
                                                                                  
               while also highlighting the imperative of creating scalable backend systems for
                                                                                  
               adequately addressing and maintaining real-time public transportation information in
                                                                                  
               the Philippines.                                                   
                                                                                  
                    PasaHero uses QR codes for payments, which requires good lighting and
                                                                                  
               camera focus. SureCut utilizes NFC technology, which allows for a faster

               PasaHero was noted to have lower reliability ratings in real-time accuracy during
                                                                                  
               testing; SureCut aims to address this by using a lightweight realtime database and
                                                                                  
               manual driver status updates (Color-coded capacity) to ensure data accuracy even
                                                                                  
               with variable internet speeds.

               Jeepney Queuing and Tracking System (JEEPQTS)                      
                                                                                  
                    The article by Sotto, Roseale B. (2023) discusses the issue in the Philippine
                                                                                  
               public transport system, where there is no real-time information present that makes it
                                                                                  
               difficult for drivers and commuters alike to know the current supply and demand flow.
                                                                                  
               To address this, the JEEPQTS project was initiated to provide real-time information
                                                                                  
               regarding Jeepney services across regions, enhancing the experience of both parties
                                                                                  
               in commuting. The project was founded on Data Collection and Analysis Methods
                                                                                  
               and underpinned by the principles of Urban Mobility and Sustainability. To make it
                                                                                  
               more accessible and economical, JEEPQTS employed SMS as its primary mode of
                                                                                  
               communication. With this, passengers and drivers could send updates or inquire
                                                                                  
               about Jeepney statuses using ordinary cell phones—eliminating the use of GPS
                                                                                  
               devices or smartphone applications. The system employed a Client-Server approach,
                                                                                  
               which facilitated all data exchange between client devices and a central database.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 55 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      34          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Both drivers and riders communicated via SMS, whereas administrators operated
                                                                                  
               routes, data, and accounts using a web-based interface.            
                                                                                  
                    On the technical front, Sotto constructed JEEPQTS utilizing simple web
                                                                                  
               technologies without any assistance from external frameworks. The web interface of
               the administrator was created using Bootstrap, in addition to HTML, CSS, and
                                                                                  
               JavaScript, whereas PHP catered to back-end operations. MySQL was utilized for
                                                                                  
               database management, and the system was deployed on Apache web servers. The
                                                                                  
               use of SMS for real-time communication was achieved through the application of
                                                                                  
               Twilio REST API, thereby facilitating seamless data exchange between users and the
                                                                                  
               system. Utilizing straightforward, inexpensive, and dependable technology, the
                                                                                  
               JEEPQTS project demonstrated how it is possible to reinvent the old Jeepney
                                                                                  
               system, making processes more orderly and efficient for commuters and drivers alike
                                                                                  
               in the Philippines.                                                
                                                                                  
                    JEEPQTS prioritizes accessibility in low-tech environments by removing the
                                                                                  
               need for internet/GPS maps. SureCut prioritizes User Experience (UX) and
                                                                                  
               Visualization. By utilizing 4G/internet and GPS, SureCut provides a visual map
                                                                                  
               interface that is easier for modern commuters to understand than SMS text updates.
                                                                                  
               SureCut targets the "pro user" and modernized units capable of running Android
                                                                                  
               apps, offering a richer feature set (live maps, color-coded occupancy) than the
                                                                                  
               text-based JEEPQTS.

                    Table 3 reveals that while studies like BUSNAV (S3), Intelliter (S4), and
                                                                                  
               Routie (S8) excel in GPS Tracking, they function primarily as standalone navigation
                                                                                  
               tools. A significant gap remains in Driver-Operator Coordination, which only
                                                                                  
               PasaHero (S6) and JEEPQTS (S10) address. Surecut advances this by digitizing
               passenger counting and remittance reporting that are absent in existing local
                                                                                  
               systems.                                                           
                                                                                  
                    Furthermore, while G2Viz (S5) offers financial reporting for backend planners,
                                                                                  
               Surecut provides real-time income data directly to the General Manager for daily
                                                                                  
               accounting. Unlike the passive data collection tools of MyAmble (S1) and Fourstep
                                                                                  
               (S2), Surecut is designed as an active operational system that synchronizes driver
                                                                                  
               performance with the cooperative’s management standards.

===== PAGE 63 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                      METHODOLOGY                                 
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    This chapter presents the requirements for developing the system and also
                                                                                  
               discusses the necessary materials used by the researchers, including the research
               design and the techniques or methods needed in developing the system.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Materials                                                          
                                                                                  
                    The material used in the development of the system consisted of a computer
                                                                                  
               for system testing. It included an HP Device equipped with an AMD Ryzen™ 5
                                                                                  
               5500U with Radeon™ Graphics @ 2.10GHz and 8 GB RAM (7.33 GB usable) on a
                                                                                  
               64-bit Windows 11 platform.                                        
                                                                                  
                    An Android smartphone was also utilized for testing the developed React
                                                                                  
               Native mobile application. The researchers used React Native as the primary
                                                                                  
               development framework, with Visual Studio Code (VS Code) as the Integrated
                                                                                  
               Development Environment (IDE), React Native as the programming language,
                                                                                  
               Node.js and npm for dependency management, and Firebase for data storage and
                                                                                  
               authentication. Figma was employed for high fidelity wireframe design, the internet
                                                                                  
               was used for information gathering, and Google Docs was utilized for documenting
                                                                                  
               the study.                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 64 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      43          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Method                                                             
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                       Figure 2. Design Thinking Methodology (Daniel Wörle, 2025) 
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The development of the Surecut application was guided by the Agile Design
                                                                                  
               Thinking methodology, which shows a cyclical, human-centered approach to
                                                                                  
               innovation. Unlike traditional linear methods, the methodology begins with empathy
                                                                                  
               and definition, requiring deep engagement with commuters and drivers to understand
                                                                                  
               their true needs and articulate the precise problems of public transport inefficiency.
                                                                                  
               Development then proceeds through rapid, iterative cycles of ideation, prototyping
                                                                                  
               and testing. The goal of each cycle is to build a high-fidelity prototype that quickly
               validates core features such as real-time tracking or optimized route suggestions
                                                                                  
               against genuine user experiences. Subsequent iterations constantly refine the
                                                                                  
               product, adjusting features and priorities based on immediate, qualitative feedback
                                                                                  
               from end-users. The greatest benefit of Agile Design Thinking methodology is its
                                                                                  
               strong focus on user validation, which ensures that the Surecut application remains
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 65 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      44          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               inherently relevant and adaptable, significantly reducing the risk of building complex
                                                                                  
               solutions that fail to meet the dynamic demands of the urban mobility sector.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Empathize                                                          
                    With the Empathize phase, the primary objective is to gain a deep,
                                                                                  
               evidence-based, and empathetic understanding of the target users by setting aside
                                                                                  
               initial assumptions (See Appendix 13. User Persona).               
                                                                                  
                    To understand the core operational challenges and commuter experiences,
                                                                                  
               the researchers conducted key informant interviews with the PTSMC Chairman,
                                                                                  
               General Manager and Drivers, (See Appendix 8, 9, 10. Interview Reports) as well as
                                                                                  
               surveys among commuters (See Appendix 6. Survey Results) who regularly ride the
                                                                                  
               Modern Jeepney cooperative route (See Appendix 14. User Journey Map). The
                                                                                  
               sessions revealed critical insights regarding the "Fixed Wage" model and the need
                                                                                  
               for visibility between driver and commuter, and digital passenger counting to validate
                                                                                  
               fuel costs. The output creates the empirical, human-driven basis of all requirements
                                                                                  
               so that the product is sought after and directly solves pain points for users.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Define                                                             
                                                                                  
                     After the dedication is set in the Empathize phase, the researchers
                                                                                  
               synthesize the gathered data to define specific pain points, such as the General
                                                                                  
               Manager’s difficulty in fleet management, the commuters’ uncertainty of jeep
                                                                                  
               availability, seat capacity, and the drivers' coordination issues during vehicle
                                                                                  
               breakdowns. The problems were mapped to specific opportunities for technological
                                                                                  
               intervention.                                                      
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 66 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      45          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Ideate                                                             
                                                                                  
                    The Ideate phase of the Design Thinking process entails the process of
                                                                                  
               generating a wide variety of potential solutions. Following on from the empathetic
               insights developed in the previous phase, the stage explicitly encourages "going
                                                                                  
               wide" to explore many possibilities without early judgment.        
                                                                                  
                    The result of this stage was a list of key solution features aimed at improving
                                                                                  
               both the driver and commuter experience. Some key concepts are using a
                                                                                  
               color-coded seat availability for commuters utilizing the application to be able to
                                                                                  
               choose whether to board the approaching Modern Jeepney or board the next.
                                                                                  
               Additionally, in order to provide real-time capability, the system provides widgets as
                                                                                  
               buttons for the driver to use so that they can send required data updates (seat
                                                                                  
               capacity) promptly. The concepts also include external sources by providing real-time
                                                                                  
               route traffic information. The researchers also brainstormed a QR code scheme for
                                                                                  
               initiating the Modern Jeepney journey, simplifying the process initiation (See
                                                                                  
               Appendix 9. Interview Report). Prototype is to convert the high-impact concepts of
                                                                                  
               the Ideate step into low-fidelity, testable prototypes (See Appendix 11. Low Fidelity
                                                                                  
               Wireframe).                                                        
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Prototype                                                          
                                                                                  
                    The primary goal of the Prototype phase is to make the proposed
                                                                                  
               features—like the real-time map interface, the notification process, and the driver
                                                                                  
               update system—presentable in the form of a demonstrable model, without investing
                                                                                  
               in final product code.                                             
                                                                                  
                    The system was developed using React Native for the mobile interface and a
               web-based dashboard for the General Manager. High-fidelity wireframes were
                                                                                  
               created to visualize the specific access levels: a "Read-Only" map view for
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 67 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      46          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               commuters to prevent data tampering, and a full "CRUD" (Create, Read, Update,
                                                                                  
               Delete) dashboard for the General Manager to oversee fleet assignments and
                                                                                  
               reports. (See Appendix 12. High Fidelity Wireframe).               
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Test                                                               
                                                                                  
                    The Test phase of Design Thinking is an iterative stage in which the
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               prototypes are presented to real users. It is an active opportunity to receive direct
               feedback, observe user interactions, and understand what does and doesn't work in
                                                                                  
               the provided solution. Its primary goal is to use the feedback to refine the prototype,
                                                                                  
               gain further empathy, and challenge assumptions. This continuous loop of testing
                                                                                  
               and refining is essential for identifying usability issues and ensuring the final solution
                                                                                  
               genuinely meets the users' needs.                                  
                                                                                  
                    In this stage, Surecut was tested first by the developers by using Test Cases,
                                                                                  
               Integration Testing and Unit Testing. After ensuring that all functionalities were
                                                                                  
               properly working, Surecut was placed directly in the hands of the commuters
                                                                                  
               (respondents), allowing them to interact with the application. Researchers have
                                                                                  
               observed the interaction, collecting feedback on usability, clarity of information, and
                                                                                  
               whether the solution effectively solved the initial problem of prediction and
                                                                                  
               uncertainty. The evaluation of the system was guided by the ISO 25010 Software
                                                                                  
               Quality Model, with particular focus on functional suitability, usability, and
                                                                                  
               performance efficiency. The quality characteristics served as the basis for analyzing
                                                                                  
               user feedback and system performance outcomes. The results were used to refine
                                                                                  
               and finalize the system design ensuring that the application meets both user
                                                                                  
               expectations and defined quality standards.                        
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 68 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                      47          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Iteration                                                          
                                                                                  
                    Iteration is a core, cyclical principle within the Design Thinking framework
                                                                                  
               rather than a discrete linear step. It embodies the non-linear nature of the entire
                                                                                  
               process, where insights and feedback gathered from the Test phase are used to
               systematically refine and improve the solution. The feedback loop often requires the
                                                                                  
               researchers to revisit earlier stages—such as Ideate (to generate new solutions
                                                                                  
               based on feedback) or Prototype (to build a refined version of the concept). The
                                                                                  
               purpose of the iterative cycles is to progressively enhance the solution's quality,
                                                                                  
               usability, and fit with user needs.                                
                                                                                  
                    The first test held in July, entailed the creation of an initial low-fidelity
                                                                                  
               wireframe in Figma (See Appendix 11. Low Fidelity Wireframe). The early-stage
                                                                                  
               prototype was presented to the PTSMC Chairman, for an initial expert review. The
                                                                                  
               feedback from the session was important and gave the researchers clear directions
                                                                                  
               regarding fundamental refinements needed and changes required at the core level
                                                                                  
               with respect to the concept and layout.                            
                                                                                  
                    From the revisions of the first cycle, the team created the second iteration in
                                                                                  
               September. Basically, it involved an updated and refined wireframe, which was then
                                                                                  
               presented to the Chairman and the General Manager, for a more comprehensive
                                                                                  
               review. The collaborative session validated the changes made and even gave further
                                                                                  
               insights into ensuring the project was up to both technical and academic standards.
                                                                                  
                    The third iteration, completed in November, marked the most significant leap,
                                                                                  
               moving from a low-fidelity design to a high-fidelity, functional prototype. The version
               consisted of an updated, fully coded user interface (UI) that integrated all three
                                                                                  
               distinct access levels: the driver, the commuter, and the operator (See Appendix 12.
                                                                                  
               High Fidelity Wireframe). The iteration represented a comprehensive model ready for
                                                                                  
               final testing and validation (See Appendix 15. Client Feedback Form).

               Statistical Treatment of Data                                      
                                                                                  
                    After the researchers manually tabulated the survey results, the following
                                                                                  
               tools were used to analyze and interpret the gathered data:        
                      1. Percentage. The percentage formula was used to determine the
                                                                                  
                         proportion of responses for each option in the survey. It was helpful in
                                                                                  
                         identifying the distribution of answers and understanding which
                                                                                  
                         experiences or situations that were most common among all
                                                                                  
                         respondents.                                             
                                                                                  
                         The Formula is:                                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                         Where:                                                   
                                                                                  
                         P = percentage                                           
                                                                                  
                         f = frequency                                            
                                                                                  
                         n = total number of respondents

                         representative value.                                    
                                                                                  
                         The Formula is:                                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                         Where:                                                   
                                                                                  
                          = weighted mean                                         
                                                                                  
                         f = frequency of each response                           
                         i                                                        
                         x = value assigned to each response                      
                         i                                                        
                         N = total number of respondents                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                      3. Slovin’s Formula. It was used to determine the appropriate number
                                                                                  
                         of respondents needed for the study.                     
                                                                                  
                         The Formula is:                                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                         Where:                                                   
                                                                                  
                         e = margin of error                                      
                                                                                  
                         n = the required sample size                             
                                                                                  
                         N = the total population size

                         system software. The scale consisted of a number from 1 to 5,

                                 RESULTS AND DISCUSSION                           
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    This chapter presents the data gathered through the research process, the
                                                                                  
               technical realization of the proposed solution, and the analysis of the results. The
               contents are structured to align with the specific objectives of the study, providing an
                                                                                  
               evidence-based narrative of how the research problems were addressed.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               System Concept and Requirements                                    
                                                                                  
                    The Surecut: Vehicle Tracking and Management System was developed to
                                                                                  
               modernize public transportation operations, enhance fleet monitoring, and facilitate
                                                                                  
               cashless transactions for the Pangkabuhayan Transport Service and Multi-Purpose
                                                                                  
               Cooperative (PTSMC). The system is designed for both commuters and drivers,
                                                                                  
               utilizing React Native and TypeScript for the Android mobile application, and React.js
                                                                                  
               with a Node.js/Express backend for the web-based Operator Dashboard. The
                                                                                  
               development process utilized the Agile Design Thinking methodology, emphasizing
                                                                                  
               client-first development, collaboration, and flexibility, particularly suitable for complex
                                                                                  
               projects.                                                          
                                                                                  
                    The Surecut mobile application has specific system requirements. Based on
                                                                                  
               the application's configuration, the minimum requirements include Android 7.0 (API
                                                                                  
               Level 24) or higher, 3 GB RAM, 500 MB of free storage, and an active internet
                                                                                  
               connection for real-time tracking. Recommended requirements are Android 11 or
                                                                                  
               higher (API Level 30+), 4 GB RAM, 1 GB of free storage, and a reliable internet
                                                                                  
               connection (Wi-Fi or 4G/5G). Hardware necessities heavily rely on an NFC (Near
                                                                                  
               Field Communication) module for tap-to-pay wallet functionalities, a GPS module for
                                                                                  
               location tracking, and mobile data connectivity.                   
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 73 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                       52         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The mobile app requires various system permissions to function optimally:
                                                                                  
               INTERNET      for     real-time   database    synchronization,     
                                                                                  
               ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION for continuous driver presence tracking even
                                                                                  
               when   the  app   is  minimized, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION  and         
               ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION for precise Google Maps route tracking, ETA 
                                                                                  
               calculations, and NFC to facilitate digital wallet payments.       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    For the web system (General Manager Dashboard), client-side requirements
                                                                                  
               include modern web browsers like Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox,
                                                                                  
               or Safari supporting modern JavaScript frameworks. The backend API requires a
                                                                                  
               Node.js runtime environment. The database setup involves configuring a Firebase
                                                                                  
               project with Firestore for persistent data (users, ride history, vehicles), Realtime
                                                                                  
               Database for live driver online/offline presence tracking, and Firebase Storage for
                                                                                  
               safekeeping driver credentials and LTFRB fare matrix documents.    
                                                                                  
                    The minimum server requirements for hosting the backend API (via platforms
                                                                                  
               like Vercel or dedicated servers) include a Linux/Windows operating system, a
                                                                                  
               dual-core CPU, 2 GB RAM, and 10 GB of disk space. Recommended server
                                                                                  
               requirements are a quad-core CPU or better, 4 GB RAM, and 20 GB of disk space to
                                                                                  
               handle concurrent real-time polling from the mobile apps. Firestore and Realtime
                                                                                  
               Database setups require enabling the Firebase Blaze (pay-as-you-go) plan to
                                                                                  
               support automated server functions and Google Maps API integrations.
                                                                                  
                    Operating primarily along the transit corridors of Molino Road and Daang Hari
                                                                                  
               connecting to Southmall and Paliparan, PTSMC faces operational challenges related
                                                                                  
               to manual fleet monitoring, traditional fare collection, and inefficient End-of-Day
                                                                                  
               (EOD) financial auditing. The rapid modernization of public utility vehicles (PUVs)
                                                                                  
               demands a digital solution to streamline cooperative processes, prompting the
                                                                                  
               development of the Surecut system to assist both the cooperative management and
                                                                                  
               the daily commuters.                                               
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 74 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                       53         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The application serves as a centralized platform for tracking fleet locations,
                                                                                  
               processing cashless payments, and generating automated financial reports. For
                                                                                  
               commuters, it offers real-time vehicle tracking powered by Google Maps, precise ETA
                                                                                  
               calculations, an integrated SOS emergency contact feature, and an NFC tap-to-pay
               wallet system ensuring a safer and more convenient travel experience. For
                                                                                  
               cooperative operators, it provides a comprehensive live map of active units, dynamic
                                                                                  
               fare configuration, and automated PDF generation for Master EOD settlements and
                                                                                  
               route income reports, empowering the management to make transparent, data-driven
                                                                                  
               decisions.                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               Design Specification and Coding                                    
                                                                                  
                    The system development was executed using a modern full-stack 
                                                                                  
               architecture. The web-based Operator Dashboard was built using React 18 and
                                                                                  
               Tailwind CSS for the frontend, while the backend was implemented with Node.js and
                                                                                  
               Express. This centralized dashboard facilitates administrative control over the entire
               system. The system incorporates three primary access levels: Administrator
                                                                                  
               (Operator), Driver and Commuter (End-User).                        
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                    The mobile application was developed using React Native and TypeScript
                                                                                  
               within Android Studio 2023 and Visual Studio Code, enabling cross-platform
                                                                                  
               functionality with a focus on Android Development. Data management was handled
                                                                                  
               by Firebase, specifically utilizing Cloud Firestore for real-time document storage,
                                                                                  
               Firebase Authentication for secure user access, Realtime Database for driver and
                                                                                  
               commuter presence tracking, and Firebase Storage for managing driver and
                                                                                  
               commuter information such as photos and ride history.              
                                                                                  
                    The system implements a contactless “Tap to Pay” feature by leveraging the
                                                                                  
               NFC (Near Field Communication) hardware native to modern Android devices. The
                                                                                  
               mobile application utilizes the react-native-nfc-manager library to interface directly
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  

===== PAGE 75 =====
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                       54         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
               with the devices’s NFC chip allowing it to act as both a reader and a tag emulator for
                                                                                  
               payment processing. Once the hardware successfully “taps”, the application triggers
                                                                                  
               a secure payment utility through the commuter’s integrated digital wallet that uses
                                                                                  
               Paymongo API that supports multiple providers, including GCash, Maya and Bank
               transactions for cash in. The payment will then be recorded under the Driver’s name
                                                                                  
               but is directly stored in the Operator’s Dashboard.
